correctness.rationale: The frozen RESULT.md gives an exhaustive finite theorem for every inverse-closed Cayley connection set of each finite abelian group of order <16. Independent re-enumeration of 20 group presentations verified all 821 inversion-orbit masks and, without trusting the checker exit status, every one of 4936 saved root-fixing automorphism permutations against the complete adjacency matrices, confirming refinement-class transitivity. A separately reconstructed 16-vertex adjacency matrix has degree 6, exactly two common neighbours for each distinct pair and rooted cells 1/6/9; amongst the nine nonneighbours the root/common-neighbour-pair adjacency invariant splits 3 vs 6. Finite exhaustion is valid here because the group list and all inverse-closed subsets are exhaustive, not an extrapolation.
residual_risks: Certificate exhaustive over listed finite abelian presentations and connection sets. It does not extend to nonabelian graphs, graphs of order >15, several individualizations or graph identification.

originality.rationale: The classical order-16 rooted failure was already established; only the all-abelian lower bound through order 15 is assessed as new. Kluge 2022 proves prime-order circulant Tinhofer behaviour and supplies a Z4×Z4 obstruction, but not a complete lower census of every smaller abelian group. Arvind et al. develop general individualization/refinement notions, not this sharp low-order minimum. Semantic and exact-term searches located no dominating earlier all-abelian lower-bound theorem; this is best-of-knowledge, not certified priority.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite graph census might already imply the minimum. Kluge section 4.3 displays intermediate rooted classes incompatible with the direct SRG rooted equitable cells for the identical generator list; the independent adjacency/certificate check is authoritative for the present exact 1-WL convention, but the literature presentation difference merits manual follow-up.

value.rationale: A sharp least-order obstruction across all finite abelian Cayley groups is a natural finite classification boundary, not an arbitrary small slice. The universal lower half is a nontrivial exhaustive combinatorial theorem with checked automorphism certificates; the known exceptional graph alone would not determine minimality. This is a reusable exact calibration example for rooted colour refinement, despite absence of an all-order theorem.
residual_risks: Natural finite threshold; finite exhaustive approach has limited scaling; no claim of completely classifying all Cayley graphs.
